title: Palindrome Permutation II
summary: Given a string s , return all unique palindromic permutations of s (if any).
statement: Given a string s , return all unique palindromic permutations of s (if any). The permutations should be listed in any order. If no palindromic permutation of s exists, return an empty list.
constraints: Return every unique palindromic permutation that uses all characters, in any order. Return an empty list when none exists.
reference_solution:
def generate_palindromes(s):
    counts = Counter(s)
    odd = [character for character, count in counts.items() if count % 2]
    if len(odd) > 1:
        return []
    center = odd[0] if odd else ""
    characters = sorted(counts)
    half_length = len(s) // 2
    answer = []
    path = []
    def build():
        if len(path) == half_length:
            left = "".join(path)
            answer.append(left + center + left[::-1])
            return
        for character in characters:
            if counts[character] >= 2:
                counts[character] -= 2
                path.append(character)
                build()
                path.pop()
                counts[character] += 2
    build()
    return answer

hints: First apply the odd-frequency rule from Palindrome Permutation.
Choose only the left half; the right half is forced as its reverse.
Backtrack over characters with at least two remaining copies, consume two, recurse, then restore them.
Choosing by character count rather than occurrence index prevents duplicate answers when letters repeat.
editorial: At most one odd-frequency letter becomes the fixed center. Every other count contributes half its copies to the left side. Backtracking chooses a character pair at each depth; mirroring the completed half creates one full palindrome. Counts make identical occurrences indistinguishable, so each unique half is generated once. The independent oracle enumerates all half permutations and deduplicates them with a set.
